title.zh: 卷八十五 志第三十五: 百官一
title.raw: 卷八十五 志第三十五: 百官一 Volume 85 Treatises 38: Official Posts 1

sentences.zh: 百官一

translations.literal: Official Posts 1
translations.idiomatic: Official Posts, Part One

sentences.zh: 王者南面以聽天下之治，建邦啟土，設官分職，其制尚矣。

translations.literal: The king faces south to hear the governance of all under Heaven, establishes states and opens territories, sets up offices and divides duties — such institutions have been esteemed since antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Since ancient times, rulers have faced south to preside over the realm, founded states and granted fiefs, and established offices with defined responsibilities — a system long held in high regard.

sentences.zh: 漢、唐以來，雖沿革不同，恒因周、秦之故，以為損益，亦無大相遠。

translations.literal: Since the Han and Tang, although there were differences in succession and change, they constantly took Zhou and Qin precedents as the basis for additions and reductions, and were not greatly divergent.
translations.idiomatic: From Han and Tang onward, though each dynasty altered the structure in its own way, all drew on Zhou and Qin models for revision, and the overall framework did not differ greatly.

sentences.zh: 大要欲得賢才用之，以佐天子、理萬民也。

translations.literal: The essential aim was to obtain talented men and employ them to assist the Son of Heaven and govern the myriad people.
translations.idiomatic: In essence, the purpose was to recruit able men to aid the emperor and administer the affairs of the people.

sentences.zh: 元太祖起自朔土，統有其眾，部落野處，非有城郭之制，國俗淳厚，非有庶事之繁，惟以萬戶統軍旅，以斷事官治政刑，任用者不過一二親貴重臣耳。

translations.literal: Yuan Taizu rose from the northern frontier, united his people, and the tribes dwelt in the wild without walled cities; the national customs were simple and thick, without the complexity of many affairs — only myriarchs commanded the armies, and judicial officials handled government and punishments; those employed were no more than one or two close and honored ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu of the Yuan rose from the northern steppe and united his followers. The tribes lived as nomads without walled towns; their ways were plain and unadorned, and daily administration was not elaborate. Armies were led by commanders of ten thousand households, while judicial officers handled law and government — and only one or two kinsmen and favored ministers were ever put in charge.

sentences.zh: 及取中原，太宗始立十路宣課司，選儒術用之。

translations.literal: When they took the Central Plains, Taizong first established the Ten Circuits Taxation Commission and selected men versed in Confucian learning to employ them.
translations.idiomatic: After the conquest of China proper, Taizong set up the Ten Circuits Taxation Commission and began appointing scholars trained in the Confucian tradition.

sentences.zh: 金人來歸者，因其故官，若行省，若元帥，則以行省、元帥授之。

translations.literal: For Jin people who came over in submission, according to their former offices — if circuit intendant, if marshal — they were granted circuit intendant or marshal posts.
translations.idiomatic: Jin defectors were given titles matching their former ranks — provincial commissioners or marshals received those same designations.

sentences.zh: 草創之初，固未暇為經久之規矣。

translations.literal: In the first days of founding, they truly had no leisure to make lasting regulations.
translations.idiomatic: In those early years of state-building, there was scarcely time to devise institutions meant to endure.

sentences.zh: 世祖即位，登用老成，大新制作，立朝儀，造都邑，遂命劉秉忠、許衡酌古今之宜，定內外之官。

translations.literal: When Shizu took the throne, he employed seasoned men, greatly renewed institutions, established court ritual, and built the capital; he then ordered Liu Bingzhong and Xu Heng to weigh what was fitting in ancient and modern times and define the offices within and without.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizu acceded, he promoted seasoned officials, overhauled institutions, established court ritual, and built the capital; he then had Liu Bingzhong and Xu Heng weigh ancient and modern precedents and define the bureaucracy at court and beyond.

sentences.zh: 其總政務者曰中書省，秉兵柄者曰樞密院，司黜陟者曰御史臺。

translations.literal: What held overall governance was called the Secretariat; what held military authority was called the Privy Council; what handled promotions and dismissals was called the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: Overall governance rested with the Secretariat, military authority with the Privy Council, and promotions and dismissals with the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 體統既立，其次在內者，則有寺，有監，有衞，有府；

translations.literal: Once the framework was established, within there were directorates, commissions, guards, and offices;
translations.idiomatic: Once the framework was in place, internal agencies included directorates, commissions, guards, and offices;

sentences.zh: 在外者，則有行省，有行臺，有宣慰司，有廉訪司。

translations.literal: without there were branch secretariats, branch censorates, pacification commissions, and surveillance commissions.
translations.idiomatic: while external ones included branch secretariats, branch censorates, pacification commissions, and surveillance commissions.

sentences.zh: 其牧民者，則曰路，曰府，曰州，曰縣。

translations.literal: Those governing the people were called circuits, prefectures, departments, and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Local administration was organized as circuits, prefectures, departments, and counties.

sentences.zh: 官有常職，位有常員，其長則蒙古人為之，而漢人、南人貳焉。

translations.literal: Offices had fixed duties and posts had fixed numbers; their chiefs were Mongols, while Han and southern Chinese served as deputies.
translations.idiomatic: Each office had fixed duties and each post a fixed quota; Mongols held the chief posts, while Han and southern Chinese served as deputies.

sentences.zh: 於是一代之制始備，百年之間，子孫有所憑藉矣。

translations.literal: Thus the institutions of the dynasty were first made complete, and for a century thereafter descendants had something to rely upon.
translations.idiomatic: In this way the dynasty's institutions were first fully established, giving later generations a foundation to rely upon for a century.

sentences.zh: 大德以後，承平日久，彌文之習勝，而質簡之意微，僥幸之門多，而方正之路塞。

translations.literal: After the Dade era, long peace prevailed; the habit of excessive refinement prevailed while the spirit of simplicity waned; doors of opportunism multiplied while the path of integrity was blocked.
translations.idiomatic: After the Dade reign, prolonged peace bred a taste for ornament over substance, opened many doors to favor-seeking, and closed the way to upright service.

sentences.zh: 官冗於上，吏肆於下，言事者屢疏論列，而朝廷訖莫正之，勢固然也。

translations.literal: Offices were redundant above and clerks ran riot below; memorialists repeatedly submitted critiques in sequence, yet the court in the end never corrected it — such was the force of circumstance.
translations.idiomatic: Posts multiplied at the top while clerks abused their power below. Critics submitted memorial after memorial, yet the court never remedied the abuse — a situation that had become all but inevitable.

sentences.zh: 大抵元之建官，繁簡因乎時，得失系乎人，故取其簡牘所載，而論次之。

translations.literal: Generally, in the Yuan establishment of offices, complexity or simplicity followed the times, and success or failure depended on the men — therefore what is recorded in the documents is taken and set forth in order.
translations.idiomatic: Broadly speaking, the Yuan bureaucracy grew or shrank with the times, and its merits or flaws depended on who held office. What follows is drawn from the archival record and arranged in order.

sentences.zh: 若其因事而置，事已則罷，與夫異教雜流世襲之屬，名類實繁，亦姑舉其大概。

translations.literal: As for those established for particular affairs and abolished when the affair ended, and those of heterodox faiths, mixed professions, and hereditary lines — the names and categories are truly numerous — only their general outline is noted here.
translations.idiomatic: Offices created for temporary needs and dissolved when those needs ended, together with posts tied to foreign religions, miscellaneous trades, and hereditary lines — though their titles and types are legion — are here summarized only in outline.

sentences.zh: 作《百官志》。

translations.literal: This composes the Treatise on Official Posts.
translations.idiomatic: Thus is composed the Treatise on Official Posts.

sentences.zh: 三公，太師、太傅、太保各一員，正一品，銀印，以道燮陰陽，經邦國。

translations.literal: The Three Dukes — Grand Preceptor, Grand Tutor, and Grand Protector, one post each, rank 1a, silver seal — harmonize yin and yang by the Way and govern the state.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Dukes — the Grand Preceptor, Grand Tutor, and Grand Protector — each one post, rank 1a, bearing a silver seal, were charged with harmonizing yin and yang and overseeing the realm.

sentences.zh: 有元襲其名號，特示尊崇。

translations.literal: The Yuan inherited their titles merely to show honor and respect.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuan adopted these titles chiefly as marks of supreme honor.

sentences.zh: 太祖十二年，以國王置太師一員。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Taizu, one Grand Preceptor was appointed with the title of king of a state.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Taizu, a Grand Preceptor was appointed and given the title of king.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，建三公，其拜罷歲月，皆不可考。

translations.literal: When Taizong took the throne, the Three Dukes were established, but the dates of their appointments and dismissals cannot be verified.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong established the Three Dukes upon his accession, but the dates of their appointments and removals cannot be determined.

sentences.zh: 世祖之世，其職常缺，而僅置太保一員。

translations.literal: In Shizu's time these posts were usually vacant, and only one Grand Protector was appointed.
translations.idiomatic: Under Shizu the posts usually stood empty; only a single Grand Protector was appointed.

sentences.zh: 至成宗、武宗而後，三公並建，而無虛位矣。

translations.literal: From Chengzong and Wuzong onward, all three dukes were established together, and there were no vacant posts.
translations.idiomatic: From the reigns of Chengzong and Wuzong onward, all three dukes were regularly filled, leaving no vacancy.

sentences.zh: 又有所謂大司徒、司徒、太尉之屬，或置，或不置。

translations.literal: There were also the so-called Grand Minister of Education, Minister of Education, and Grand Commandant — sometimes appointed, sometimes not.
translations.idiomatic: There were also posts such as Grand Minister of Education, Minister of Education, and Grand Commandant, which were sometimes filled and sometimes left vacant.

sentences.zh: 其置者，或開府，或不開府。

translations.literal: When appointed, some were granted establishment of a bureau, some were not.
translations.idiomatic: When these posts existed, some holders were authorized to maintain a staff bureau and some were not.

sentences.zh: 而東宮嘗置三師、三少，蓋亦不恒有也。

translations.literal: The Eastern Palace sometimes had the Three Masters and Three Mentors established — but these too were not constant.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince's household sometimes had Three Masters and Three Mentors as well, though these too were not permanently maintained.

sentences.zh: 中書令一員，銀印，典領百官，會決庶務。

translations.literal: Director of the Secretariat, one post, silver seal — directs all officials and convenes to decide general affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of the Secretariat — one post, silver seal — oversaw all officials and convened to decide routine state business.

sentences.zh: 太宗以相臣為之，世祖以皇太子兼之。

translations.literal: Taizong had a chief minister hold the post; Shizu had the crown prince hold it concurrently.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong assigned the post to his chief minister; Shizu had the crown prince hold it in addition to his other duties.

sentences.zh: 至元十年，立皇太子，行中書令。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Zhiyuan, the crown prince was established and acted as Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Zhiyuan (1273), a crown prince was installed and served as acting Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 大德十一年，以皇太子領中書令。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Dade, the crown prince was made to head the Directorate of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Dade (1307), the crown prince was placed in charge of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 延祐三年，復以皇太子行中書令。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yanyou, again the crown prince acted as Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yanyou (1316), the crown prince again served as acting Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 置屬，監印二人。

translations.literal: Subordinates were appointed: two seal supervisors.
translations.idiomatic: Subordinates included two seal supervisors.

sentences.zh: 右丞相、左丞相各一員，正一品，銀印，統六官，率百司，居令之次。

translations.literal: Right Chancellor and Left Chancellor, one post each, rank 1a, silver seal — command the Six Ministries, lead the hundred offices, and rank next after the Director.
translations.idiomatic: The Right Chancellor and Left Chancellor — one each, rank 1a, silver seal — commanded the Six Ministries, directed the hundred offices, and stood immediately below the Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 令缺，則總省事，佐天子，理萬機。

translations.literal: When the Director was vacant, they took overall charge of Secretariat affairs, assisted the Son of Heaven, and handled the myriad tasks of state.
translations.idiomatic: When the Directorate stood vacant, they assumed its duties, assisted the emperor, and managed the affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 國初，職名未創，太宗始置右丞相一員、左丞相一員。

translations.literal: At the founding of the state the title had not yet been created; Taizong first appointed one Right Chancellor and one Left Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: In the earliest days the title did not yet exist; Taizong was the first to appoint one Right Chancellor and one Left Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 世祖中統元年，置丞相一員。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhongtong under Shizu, one Chancellor was appointed.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhongtong (1260), Shizu appointed a single Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 二年，復置右丞相二員、左丞相二員。

translations.literal: In the second year, two Right Chancellors and two Left Chancellors were again appointed.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, two Right Chancellors and two Left Chancellors were restored.

sentences.zh: 至元二年，增置丞相五員。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhiyuan, five additional Chancellors were appointed.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhiyuan (1265), five additional Chancellors were added.

sentences.zh: 七年，立尚書省，置丞相二員。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, the Department of State Affairs was established and two Chancellors were appointed.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year (1270), the Department of State Affairs was created with two Chancellors.

sentences.zh: 八年，罷尚書省，乃置丞相二員。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, the Department of State Affairs was abolished, and two Chancellors were then appointed.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year (1271), the Department was abolished and two Chancellors were appointed to the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，復立尚書省，其中書省丞相二員如故。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, the Department of State Affairs was re-established; the two Chancellors of the Secretariat remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year (1287), the Department was re-established while the Secretariat retained its two Chancellors.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，以尚書再罷，專任一相。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, with the Department again abolished, a single Chancellor alone was appointed.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year (1292), the Department was abolished again and a single Chancellor was appointed.

sentences.zh: 武宗至大二年，復置尚書省，丞相二員，中書丞相二員。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhida under Wuzong, the Department of State Affairs was restored — two Chancellors for it and two for the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhida (1309), Wuzong restored the Department with two Chancellors, while the Secretariat also had two.

sentences.zh: 四年，尚書省仍歸中書，丞相凡二員，自後因之不易。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, the Department was merged back into the Secretariat; Chancellors totaled two posts, and thereafter this remained unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year (1311), the Department was merged back into the Secretariat, leaving two Chancellors in all — a arrangement that thereafter remained fixed.

sentences.zh: 文宗至順元年，專任右相，其一或置或不置。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhishun under Wenzong, only the Right Chancellor was regularly appointed; the other post was sometimes filled and sometimes not.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhishun (1330), Wenzong relied chiefly on the Right Chancellor alone; the Left Chancellor was sometimes appointed and sometimes left vacant.

sentences.zh: 平章政事四員，從一品，掌機務，貳丞相，凡軍國重事，無不由之。

translations.literal: Administrators of Affairs, four posts, rank 1b — handle state business, assist the Chancellors; all important military and state matters pass through them.
translations.idiomatic: Administrators of Affairs — four posts, rank 1b — managed routine state business and assisted the Chancellors; all weighty military and civil matters passed through them.

sentences.zh: 世祖中統元年，置平章二員。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhongtong under Shizu, two Administrators were appointed.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhongtong (1260), two Administrators of Affairs were appointed.

sentences.zh: 二年，置平章四員。

translations.literal: In the second year, four Administrators were appointed.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, the number was raised to four.

sentences.zh: 至元七年，置尚書省，設尚書平章二員。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Zhiyuan, the Department of State Affairs was established with two Administrators for the Department.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Zhiyuan (1270), the Department of State Affairs was created with two of its own Administrators.

sentences.zh: 八年，尚書並入中書，平章復設三員。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, the Department was merged into the Secretariat and three Administrators were again appointed.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year (1271), the Department was absorbed into the Secretariat and three Administrators were appointed there.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，詔清冗職，平章汰為二員。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, an edict ordered the elimination of redundant posts; Administrators were reduced to two.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year (1286), an edict culled redundant offices and reduced Administrators to two.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，復尚書省，中書、尚書兩省平章各二員。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, the Department was restored; each of the Secretariat and Department had two Administrators.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year (1287), the Department was restored, with two Administrators in each of the Secretariat and the Department.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，罷尚書省，增中書平章為五員，而一員為商議省事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, the Department was abolished; Secretariat Administrators were increased to five, one of whom was for deliberation on Secretariat affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year (1292), the Department was abolished and the Secretariat's Administrators were increased to five, one designated for deliberation on Secretariat business.

sentences.zh: 三十年，又增平章為六員。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year, Administrators were again increased to six.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year (1293), the number was raised again to six.

sentences.zh: 成宗元貞元年，改商議省事為平章軍國重事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanzhen under Chengzong, the deliberator on Secretariat affairs was renamed Administrator of Important Military and State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yuanzhen (1295), the deliberator's title was changed to Administrator of Important Military and State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 武宗至大二年，再立尚書省，平章三員，中書五員。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhida under Wuzong, the Department was again established — three Administrators for it and five for the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhida (1309), Wuzong re-established the Department with three Administrators, while the Secretariat had five.

sentences.zh: 四年，罷尚書省歸中書，平章仍五員。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, the Department was abolished and merged into the Secretariat; Administrators remained at five.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year (1311), the Department was abolished and merged back into the Secretariat, which retained five Administrators.

sentences.zh: 文宗至順元年，定置四員，自後因之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhishun under Wenzong, four posts were fixed, and thereafter this remained unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhishun (1330), the number was fixed at four, and this arrangement thereafter held.

sentences.zh: 右丞一員，正二品，左丞一員，正二品，副宰相裁成庶務，號左右轄。

translations.literal: Right Vice-Director, one post, rank 2a; Left Vice-Director, one post, rank 2a — assist the chancellors in completing general affairs, styled the Left and Right Assistants.
translations.idiomatic: The Right Vice-Director and Left Vice-Director — one each, rank 2a — assisted the chancellors in managing routine affairs and were known as the Left and Right Assistants.

sentences.zh: 世祖中統二年，置左、右丞各一員。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhongtong under Shizu, one Left and one Right Vice-Director were appointed.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhongtong (1261), one Left and one Right Vice-Director were appointed.

sentences.zh: 三年，增為四員。

translations.literal: In the third year, the number was increased to four.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, the number was increased to four.

sentences.zh: 至元七年，立尚書省，中書右丞、左丞仍四員。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Zhiyuan, the Department of State Affairs was established; the Secretariat's Right and Left Vice-Directors remained at four posts.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Zhiyuan (1270), the Department was established; the Secretariat still had four Vice-Directors.

sentences.zh: 八年，尚書並入中書省，右、左丞各一員。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, the Department was merged into the Secretariat; one Right and one Left Vice-Director each.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year (1271), the Department was absorbed and the Secretariat had one Right and one Left Vice-Director.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，汰冗職，右、左丞如故。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, redundant posts were eliminated; Right and Left Vice-Directors remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year (1286), redundant offices were cut, but the Vice-Directors remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，復立尚書省，右、左丞各一，而中書省缺員。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, the Department was re-established with one Right and one Left Vice-Director each, while the Secretariat had vacant posts.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year (1287), the Department was restored with one Right and one Left Vice-Director, while the Secretariat's posts stood vacant.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，復罷尚書省。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year, the Department of State Affairs was again abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year (1291), the Department was abolished once more.

sentences.zh: 三十年，設右丞二員，而一員為商議省事。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year, two Right Vice-Directors were appointed, one of whom was for deliberation on Secretariat affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year (1293), two Right Vice-Directors were appointed, one designated for deliberation on Secretariat business.

sentences.zh: 成宗元貞元年，右丞商議省事者，又以昭文大學士與中書省事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanzhen under Chengzong, the Right Vice-Director who deliberated on Secretariat affairs was also given the title of Grand Academician of the Hall for the Diffusion of Literature and shared Secretariat duties.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yuanzhen (1295), the Right Vice-Director who handled deliberation was also made Grand Academician of the Hall for the Diffusion of Literature and shared Secretariat duties.

sentences.zh: 武宗至大二年，復立尚書省，右、左丞二員，中書右、左丞五員。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhida under Wuzong, the Department was re-established with two Right and Left Vice-Directors; the Secretariat had five.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhida (1309), the Department was restored with two Vice-Directors, while the Secretariat had five.

sentences.zh: 四年，罷尚書右、左丞，中書右、左丞止設四員。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, the Department's Right and Left Vice-Directors were abolished; the Secretariat's were fixed at four posts.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year (1311), the Department's Vice-Directors were abolished and the Secretariat's were reduced to four.

sentences.zh: 文宗至順元年，定置右丞一員、左丞一員，而由是不復增損。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhishun under Wenzong, one Right and one Left Vice-Director were fixed, and thereafter no further additions or reductions were made.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhishun (1330), one Right and one Left Vice-Director were fixed, and the number was never changed again.

sentences.zh: 參政二員，從二品，副宰相以參大政，而其職亞於右、左丞。

translations.literal: Participating Administrators, two posts, rank 2b — assist the chancellors in great affairs of state, their duties ranking below the Right and Left Vice-Directors.
translations.idiomatic: Participating Administrators — two posts, rank 2b — assisted the chancellors in major policy, ranking below the Right and Left Vice-Directors.

sentences.zh: 世祖中統元年，始置參政一員。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhongtong under Shizu, one Participating Administrator was first appointed.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhongtong (1260), a single Participating Administrator was first appointed.

sentences.zh: 二年，增為二員。

translations.literal: In the second year, the number was increased to two.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, the number was raised to two.

sentences.zh: 至元七年，立尚書省，參政三員。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Zhiyuan, the Department of State Affairs was established with three Participating Administrators.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Zhiyuan (1270), the Department was created with three Participating Administrators.

sentences.zh: 八年，尚書並入中書，參政二員。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, the Department was merged into the Secretariat; two Participating Administrators.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year (1271), the Department was absorbed and the Secretariat had two Participating Administrators.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，汰冗職，參政二員如故。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, redundant posts were eliminated; two Participating Administrators remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year (1286), redundant offices were cut, but two Participating Administrators remained.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，復立尚書省，參政二員，中書參政二員。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, the Department was re-established with two Participating Administrators; the Secretariat also had two.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year (1287), the Department was restored with two Participating Administrators, as did the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，罷尚書省參政。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year, the Department's Participating Administrators were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year (1291), the Department's Participating Administrators were abolished.

sentences.zh: 武宗至大二年，復置尚書省，參政二員，中書參政二員。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhida under Wuzong, the Department was restored with two Participating Administrators; the Secretariat also had two.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhida (1309), the Department was restored with two Participating Administrators, as did the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 四年，並尚書省入中書，參政三員。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, the Department was merged into the Secretariat; three Participating Administrators.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year (1311), the Department was merged into the Secretariat, which then had three Participating Administrators.

sentences.zh: 文宗至順元年，定參政為二員，自後因之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhishun under Wenzong, Participating Administrators were fixed at two posts, and thereafter this remained unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhishun (1330), the number was fixed at two, and this arrangement thereafter held.

sentences.zh: 參議中書省事，秩正四品。

translations.literal: Counselor of Secretariat Affairs, rank 4a.
translations.idiomatic: The Counselor of Secretariat Affairs held rank 4a.

sentences.zh: 典左右司文牘，為六曹之管轄，軍國重事咸預決焉。

translations.literal: He managed the documents of the Left and Right Offices, supervised the Six Sections, and participated in all decisions on important military and state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He managed Left and Right Office documents, supervised the Six Sections, and took part in all major military and state decisions.

sentences.zh: 中統元年，始置一員。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhongtong, one post was first established.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhongtong, one post was first established.

sentences.zh: 至元二十二年，累增至六員。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year of Zhiyuan, the number was gradually increased to six.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year of Zhiyuan, the number was gradually increased to six.

sentences.zh: 大德元年，止置四員，後遂為定額。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dade, the number was fixed at four, and this thereafter became the permanent quota.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Dade, the establishment was fixed at four, which thereafter became the permanent quota.

sentences.zh: 其治曰參議府，令史二人。

translations.literal: Its office was called the Counselorate, with two clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Its office was called the Counselorate, with two clerks.

sentences.zh: 左司，郎中二員，正五品；

translations.literal: Left Secretariat Office: two Directors, rank 5a;
translations.idiomatic: The Left Secretariat Office: two Directors, rank 5a;

sentences.zh: 員外郎二員，正六品；

translations.literal: two Vice Directors, rank 6a;
translations.idiomatic: two Vice Directors, rank 6a;

sentences.zh: 都事二員，正七品。

translations.literal: two Secretaries, rank 7a.
translations.idiomatic: two Secretaries, rank 7a.

sentences.zh: 中統元年，置左右司。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhongtong, the Left and Right Secretariat Offices were established.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhongtong (1260), the Left and Right Secretariat Offices were established.

sentences.zh: 至元十五年，分置兩司。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Zhiyuan, the two offices were separately established.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Zhiyuan (1278), they were formally separated into two distinct offices.

sentences.zh: 左司所掌：吏禮房之科有九，一曰南吏，二曰北吏，三曰貼黃，四曰保舉，五曰禮，六曰時政記，七曰封贈，八曰牌印，九曰好事。

translations.literal: What the Left Office controls: the Personnel and Rites Section has nine categories — (1) Southern personnel, (2) Northern personnel, (3) yellow slips, (4) recommendations, (5) rites, (6) record of current policy, (7) enfeoffment and posthumous honors, (8) plaques and seals, (9) commendations.
translations.idiomatic: The Left Office oversaw: the Personnel and Rites Section, with nine categories — (1) Southern personnel, (2) Northern personnel, (3) yellow slips, (4) recommendations, (5) rites, (6) record of current policy, (7) enfeoffment and posthumous honors, (8) plaques and seals, and (9) commendations.

sentences.zh: 知除房之科有五，一曰資品，二曰常選，三曰臺院選，四曰見闕選，五曰別裏哥選。

translations.literal: The Appointments Section has five categories — (1) qualifications and ranks, (2) regular selection, (3) censorate and court selection, (4) selection for current vacancies, (5) Belge selection.
translations.idiomatic: The Appointments Section had five categories — (1) qualifications and ranks, (2) regular selection, (3) censorate and court selection, (4) selection for current vacancies, and (5) Belge selection.

sentences.zh: 戶雜房之科有七，一曰定俸，二曰衣裝，三曰羊馬，四曰置計，五曰田土，六曰太府監，七曰會總。

translations.literal: The Household Miscellaneous Section has seven categories — (1) fixed salaries, (2) clothing, (3) sheep and horses, (4) provisioning accounts, (5) land, (6) Imperial Storehouse Directorate, (7) consolidated accounts.
translations.idiomatic: The Household Miscellaneous Section had seven categories — (1) fixed salaries, (2) clothing, (3) sheep and horses, (4) provisioning accounts, (5) land, (6) Imperial Storehouse Directorate, and (7) consolidated accounts.

sentences.zh: 科糧房之科有六，一曰海運，二曰儹運，三曰邊遠，四曰賑濟，五曰事故，六曰軍匠。

translations.literal: The Tax Grain Section has six categories — (1) sea transport, (2) porterage transport, (3) remote frontiers, (4) relief, (5) incidents, (6) military artisans.
translations.idiomatic: The Tax Grain Section had six categories — (1) sea transport, (2) porterage transport, (3) remote frontiers, (4) relief, (5) incidents, and (6) military artisans.

sentences.zh: 銀鈔房之科有二，一曰鈔法，二曰課程。

translations.literal: The Silver and Paper Money Section has two categories — (1) paper currency regulations, (2) tax items.
translations.idiomatic: The Silver and Paper Money Section had two categories — (1) paper currency regulations and (2) tax items.

sentences.zh: 應辦房之科有二，一曰飲膳，二曰草料。

translations.literal: The Provisioning Section has two categories — (1) food and drink, (2) fodder.
translations.idiomatic: The Provisioning Section had two categories — (1) food and drink and (2) fodder.

sentences.zh: 令史二人，蒙古書寫二十人，回回書寫一人，漢人書寫七人，典吏十五人。

translations.literal: Two clerks, twenty Mongol scribes, one Muslim scribe, seven Han scribes, fifteen record keepers.
translations.idiomatic: Staff included two clerks, twenty Mongol scribes, one Muslim scribe, seven Han scribes, and fifteen record keepers.

sentences.zh: 右司，郎中二員，正五品；

translations.literal: Right Secretariat Office: two Directors, rank 5a;
translations.idiomatic: The Right Secretariat Office: two Directors, rank 5a;

sentences.zh: 員外郎二員，正六品；

translations.literal: two Vice Directors, rank 6a;
translations.idiomatic: two Vice Directors, rank 6a;

sentences.zh: 都事二員，正七品。

translations.literal: two Secretaries, rank 7a.
translations.idiomatic: two Secretaries, rank 7a.

sentences.zh: 中統元年，置左右司。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhongtong, the Left and Right Secretariat Offices were established.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhongtong (1260), the Left and Right Secretariat Offices were established.

sentences.zh: 至元十五年，分置兩司。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Zhiyuan, the two offices were separately established.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Zhiyuan (1278), they were formally separated into two distinct offices.

sentences.zh: 右司所掌：兵房之科有五，一曰邊關，二曰站赤，三曰鋪馬，四曰屯田，五曰牧地。

translations.literal: What the Right Office controls: the Military Section has five categories — (1) frontier passes, (2) postal stations, (3) relay horses, (4) garrison farming, (5) pasture lands.
translations.idiomatic: The Right Office oversaw: the Military Section, with five categories — (1) frontier passes, (2) postal stations, (3) relay horses, (4) garrison farming, and (5) pasture lands.

sentences.zh: 刑房之科有六，一曰法令，二曰弭盜，三曰功賞，四曰禁治，五曰枉勘，六曰鬥訟。

translations.literal: The Punishments Section has six categories — (1) statutes, (2) suppressing banditry, (3) rewards for merit, (4) prohibitions and corrections, (5) wrongful inquests, (6) litigation.
translations.idiomatic: The Punishments Section had six categories — (1) statutes, (2) suppressing banditry, (3) rewards for merit, (4) prohibitions and corrections, (5) wrongful inquests, and (6) litigation.

sentences.zh: 工房之科有六，一曰橫造軍器，二曰常課段匹，三曰歲賜，四曰營造，五曰應辦，六曰河道。

translations.literal: The Works Section has six categories — (1) unauthorized manufacture of weapons, (2) regular tax in silk bolts, (3) annual grants, (4) construction, (5) provisioning, (6) waterways.
translations.idiomatic: The Works Section had six categories — (1) unauthorized manufacture of weapons, (2) regular tax in silk bolts, (3) annual grants, (4) construction, (5) provisioning, and (6) waterways.

sentences.zh: 令史二人，蒙古書寫三人，回回書寫一人，漢人書寫一人，典吏五人。

translations.literal: Two clerks, three Mongol scribes, one Muslim scribe, one Han scribe, five record keepers.
translations.idiomatic: Staff included two clerks, three Mongol scribes, one Muslim scribe, one Han scribe, and five record keepers.

sentences.zh: 中書省掾屬：監印二人，掌監視省印，有中書令則置。

translations.literal: Secretariat subordinates: two seal supervisors, who oversee the provincial seal — appointed when there is a Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat staff included two seal supervisors who guarded the Secretariat seal — appointed whenever a Director of the Secretariat was in office.

sentences.zh: 知印四人，掌執用省印。

translations.literal: Four seal keepers, who manage the application of the Secretariat seal.
translations.idiomatic: Four seal keepers managed use of the Secretariat seal.

sentences.zh: 怯裏馬赤四人。

translations.literal: Four keshig.
translations.idiomatic: Four keshig guards.

sentences.zh: 蒙古必阇赤二十二人，左司十六人，右司六人。

translations.literal: Twenty-two Mongol bitichi — sixteen in the Left Office, six in the Right Office.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-two Mongol bitichi (scribes): sixteen in the Left Office and six in the Right Office.

sentences.zh: 漢人省掾六十人，左司三十九人，右司二十一人。

translations.literal: Sixty Han secretariat clerks — thirty-nine in the Left Office, twenty-one in the Right Office.
translations.idiomatic: Sixty Han secretariat clerks: thirty-nine in the Left Office and twenty-one in the Right Office.

sentences.zh: 回回省掾十四人，左司九人，右司五人。

translations.literal: Fourteen Muslim secretariat clerks — nine in the Left Office, five in the Right Office.
translations.idiomatic: Fourteen Muslim secretariat clerks: nine in the Left Office and five in the Right Office.

sentences.zh: 宣使五十人。

translations.literal: Fifty emissaries.
translations.idiomatic: Fifty emissaries.

sentences.zh: 省醫三人。

translations.literal: Three secretariat physicians.
translations.idiomatic: Three secretariat physicians.

sentences.zh: 玉典赤四十一人。

translations.literal: Forty-one yudanchi.
translations.idiomatic: Forty-one yudanchi attendants.

sentences.zh: 斷事官，秩三品，掌刑政之屬。

translations.literal: Judicial commissioners, rank 3, who manage matters relating to punishments and government.
translations.idiomatic: Judicial commissioners, rank 3, oversaw criminal administration.

sentences.zh: 國初，嘗以相臣任之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the state, prime ministers were once appointed to the post.
translations.idiomatic: In the dynasty's early years, prime ministers sometimes held the office.

sentences.zh: 其名甚重，其員數增損不常，其人則皆御位下及中宮、東宮、諸王各投下怯薛丹等人為之。

translations.literal: Its title was very weighty; the number of posts increased and decreased without fixed rule; those appointed were all persons from the imperial household, the empress's household, the crown prince's household, and the various princes' appanages — keshig guards and the like.
translations.idiomatic: The title carried great prestige, but the number of posts fluctuated. Holders were drawn from the imperial household, the empress's and crown prince's establishments, and the appanages of the princes — keshig guards and men of that sort.

sentences.zh: 中統元年，一十六位下置三十一員。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhongtong, thirty-one posts were established under the sixteen households.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhongtong, thirty-one commissioners were appointed across the sixteen imperial households.

sentences.zh: 至元六年，十七位下置三十四員。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhiyuan, thirty-four posts were established under seventeen households.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Zhiyuan, the number rose to thirty-four posts across seventeen households.

sentences.zh: 七年，十八位下置三十五員。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, thirty-five posts were established under eighteen households.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, thirty-five posts were set under eighteen households.

sentences.zh: 八年，始給印。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, official seals were first issued.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, the office first received an official seal.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，分立兩省，而斷事官隨省並置。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year, the two secretariats were separately established, and judicial commissioners were concurrently established with each secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year, when the two secretariats were split, judicial commissioners were assigned to each.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，十八位下置三十六員，並入中書。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year, thirty-six posts were established under eighteen households, all incorporated into the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year, thirty-six posts were established under eighteen households and placed under the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，增二員。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year, two posts were added.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-first year, two posts were added.

sentences.zh: 後定置，自御位下及諸王位下共置四十一員。

translations.literal: Later fixed establishment: a total of forty-one posts were established under the imperial household and the various princes' households.
translations.idiomatic: The final establishment fixed forty-one posts under the imperial household and the princely households combined.

sentences.zh: 首領官：經歷一員，知事一員。

translations.literal: Leading officials: one intendant, one registrar.
translations.idiomatic: Leadership posts comprised one intendant and one registrar.

sentences.zh: 吏屬：蒙古必阇赤二人，令史一十二人，回回令史一人，怯裏馬赤二人，知印二人，奏差八人，典吏一人。

translations.literal: Clerical staff: two Mongol bitichi, twelve clerks, one Muslim clerk, two keshig, two seal keepers, eight memorial couriers, one record keeper.
translations.idiomatic: Clerical staff included two Mongol bitichi, twelve clerks, one Muslim clerk, two keshig guards, two seal keepers, eight memorial couriers, and one record keeper.

sentences.zh: 客省使，秩正五品，使四員，正五品；

translations.literal: Guest Secretariat commissioners, rank 5a; four commissioners, rank 5a;
translations.idiomatic: Guest Secretariat commissioners, rank 5a: four commissioners of rank 5a;

sentences.zh: 副使二員，正六品；

translations.literal: two vice commissioners, rank 6a;
translations.idiomatic: two vice commissioners, rank 6a;

sentences.zh: 令史一人，掌直省舍人、宣使等員選舉差遣之事。

translations.literal: One clerk, who manages the selection and dispatch of direct secretariat attendants, emissaries, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: One clerk handled selection and assignment of direct secretariat attendants, emissaries, and related staff.

sentences.zh: 至元九年，置使二員，一員兼通事，一員不兼。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Zhiyuan, two commissioners were established — one also serving as interpreter, one not.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Zhiyuan, two commissioners were appointed; one also served as interpreter, the other did not.

sentences.zh: 大德元年，增置四員，副二員。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dade, four commissioners and two vice commissioners were added.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Dade, four commissioners and two vice commissioners were added.

sentences.zh: 直省舍人二員，至元七年始置，後增至三十三員。

translations.literal: Direct secretariat attendants, two posts — first established in the seventh year of Zhiyuan, later increased to thirty-three.
translations.idiomatic: Direct secretariat attendants: first established with two posts in the seventh year of Zhiyuan, later increased to thirty-three.

sentences.zh: 掌奏事給使差遣之役。

translations.literal: They managed the duties of presenting memorials and carrying out attendant missions.
translations.idiomatic: They handled presentation of memorials and attendant missions.

sentences.zh: 檢校官四員，正七品。

translations.literal: Four inspection officers, rank 7a.
translations.idiomatic: Four inspection officers, rank 7a.

sentences.zh: 掌檢校左右司、六部公事程期、文牘稽失之事。

translations.literal: They inspected the deadlines and documentary errors of official business in the Left and Right Secretariat Offices and the Six Ministries.
translations.idiomatic: They audited deadlines and documentary lapses in the Left and Right Offices and Six Ministries.

sentences.zh: 大德元年置。

translations.literal: Established in the first year of Dade.
translations.idiomatic: They were established in the first year of Dade.

sentences.zh: 照磨一員，正八品。

translations.literal: Audit officer, one post, rank 8a.
translations.idiomatic: One audit officer, rank 8a.

sentences.zh: 掌磨勘左右司錢穀出納、營繕料例，凡數計、文牘、簿籍之事。

translations.literal: He audited the receipt and disbursement of funds and grain in the Left and Right Offices, construction material standards, and all matters of accounting, documents, and ledgers.
translations.idiomatic: He audited fiscal receipts and disbursements, construction standards, and all accounts, documents, and ledgers for the Left and Right Offices.

sentences.zh: 中統元年，置二員。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhongtong, two posts were established.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhongtong, two posts were established.

sentences.zh: 至元八年，省為一員。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Zhiyuan, reduced to one post.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Zhiyuan, the number was reduced to one.

sentences.zh: 典吏八人。

translations.literal: Eight record keepers.
translations.idiomatic: Eight record keepers.

sentences.zh: 管勾一員，正八品。

translations.literal: Registrar, one post, rank 8a.
translations.idiomatic: One registrar, rank 8a.

sentences.zh: 掌出納四方文移緘縢啟拆之事。

translations.literal: He managed receipt and dispatch of sealed documents from all quarters, opening and breaking seals.
translations.idiomatic: He handled receipt and dispatch of sealed documents from all quarters, opening and breaking seals.

sentences.zh: 郵遞之程期，曹屬之承受，兼主之。

translations.literal: He also jointly supervised postal deadlines and the reception of documents by office staff.
translations.idiomatic: He also jointly supervised postal deadlines and document reception by office staff.

sentences.zh: 中統元年，置二員。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhongtong, two posts were established.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhongtong, two posts were established.

sentences.zh: 至元八年，省為一員，典吏八人。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Zhiyuan, reduced to one post; eight record keepers.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Zhiyuan, the number was reduced to one, with eight record keepers.

sentences.zh: 架閣庫管勾二員，正八品，掌庋藏省府籍帳案牘，凡備稽考之文，即掌故之任。

translations.literal: Two archive depot registrars, rank 8a, who store and maintain the Secretariat and government household registers, ledgers, and case files — all documents kept for audit and reference; this was the archivist's charge.
translations.idiomatic: Two archive depot registrars, rank 8a, maintained the Secretariat's registers, ledgers, and case files — the archival records kept for audit. This was the archivist's role.

sentences.zh: 至元三年，始置二員，其後增置員數不一。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhiyuan, two posts were first established; thereafter the number added varied.
translations.idiomatic: First established with two posts in the third year of Zhiyuan; the number of added posts thereafter varied.

sentences.zh: 至順初，定為二員，典吏十人。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhishun, fixed at two posts; ten record keepers.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Zhishun, the establishment was fixed at two posts with ten record keepers.

sentences.zh: 蒙古架閣庫兼管勾一員，典吏二人。

translations.literal: One combined registrar for the Mongol archive depot; two record keepers.
translations.idiomatic: One combined registrar for the Mongol archive depot, with two record keepers.

sentences.zh: 回回架閣庫管勾一員，典吏二人。

translations.literal: One registrar for the Muslim archive depot; two record keepers.
translations.idiomatic: One registrar for the Muslim archive depot, with two record keepers.

sentences.zh: 吏部，尚書三員，正三品；

translations.literal: Ministry of Personnel: three ministers, rank 3a;
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Personnel: three ministers, rank 3a;

sentences.zh: 侍郎二員，正四品；

translations.literal: two vice ministers, rank 4a;
translations.idiomatic: two vice ministers, rank 4a;

sentences.zh: 郎中二員，從五品；

translations.literal: two directors, rank 5b;
translations.idiomatic: two directors, rank 5b;

sentences.zh: 員外郎二員，從六品，掌天下官吏選授之政令。

translations.literal: two vice directors, rank 6b, who manage the government's policies on selecting and appointing officials throughout the empire.
translations.idiomatic: two vice directors, rank 6b, who issued policies for selecting and appointing officials empire-wide.

sentences.zh: 凡職官銓綜之典，吏員調補之格，勛封爵邑之制，考課殿最之法，悉以任之。

translations.idiomatic: At the dynasty's founding, the Yidu Taxation Office was first established to oversee Shandong salterns and collect salt revenue; it was later converted into a transport commission.

sentences.zh: 中統四年，詔以中書左右部兼諸路都轉運司。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhongtong, an edict ordered the Left and Right Sections of the Central Secretariat to concurrently administer the Director-General Transport Commissions in all circuits.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Zhongtong, an edict ordered the Left and Right Sections of the Central Secretariat to concurrently administer the director-general transport commissions in all circuits.

sentences.zh: 至元二年，命有司兼辦其課，改立山東轉運司。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhiyuan, ordered the relevant offices to concurrently manage its revenue; the Shandong Transport Commission was established.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhiyuan, the relevant offices were ordered to manage its revenue concurrently, and the Shandong Transport Commission was established.

sentences.zh: 至元十二年，改立都轉運司。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Zhiyuan, the Director-General Transport Commission was established.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Zhiyuan, the Director-General Transport Commission was established.

sentences.zh: 延祐五年，以鹽法澀滯，降分司印，巡行各場，督收課程，罷膠萊鹽司所屬鹽場。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yanyou, because the salt laws had become stagnant, branch office seals were issued to tour the various salterns, supervise revenue collection, and abolish the salterns subordinate to the Jiaolai Salt Office.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Yanyou, because salt administration had grown stagnant, branch office seals were issued to tour the salterns, supervise revenue collection, and abolish the salterns subordinate to the Jiaolai Salt Office.

sentences.zh: 鹽場一十九所，每場設司令一員，從七品；

translations.literal: Nineteen salterns, each with one commander, rank 7b;
translations.idiomatic: There were nineteen salterns; each had one commander, rank 7b;

sentences.zh: 司丞一員，從八品；

translations.literal: one assistant director, rank 8b;
translations.idiomatic: one assistant director, rank 8b;

sentences.zh: 管勾一員，從八品。

translations.literal: one overseer, rank 8b.
translations.idiomatic: one overseer, rank 8b.

sentences.zh: 永利場，寧海場，官臺場，豐國場，新鎮場，豐民場，富國場，高家港場，永阜場，利國場，固堤場，王家岡場，信陽場，濤洛場，石河場，海滄場，行村場，登寧場，西由場。

translations.literal: Yongli Saltern, Ninghai Saltern, Guantai Saltern, Fengguo Saltern, Xinzhen Saltern, Fengmin Saltern, Fuguo Saltern, Gaojiagang Saltern, Yongfu Saltern, Liguo Saltern, Gudi Saltern, Wangjiagang Saltern, Xinyang Saltern, Taoluo Saltern, Shihe Saltern, Haicang Saltern, Xingcun Saltern, Dengning Saltern, Xiyou Saltern.
translations.idiomatic: Yongli, Ninghai, Guantai, Fengguo, Xinzhen, Fengmin, Fuguo, Gaojiagang, Yongfu, Liguo, Gudi, Wangjiagang, Xinyang, Taoluo, Shihe, Haicang, Xingcun, Dengning, and Xiyou salterns.

sentences.zh: 河東陜西等處轉運鹽使司，品秩、職掌同前，運判增一員。

translations.literal: Hedong-Shaanxi and Other Places Salt Transport Commissioner's Office — rank and duties as before, with one additional transport judge.
translations.idiomatic: The Hedong-Shaanxi and Other Places Salt Transport Commissioner's Office had the same rank and duties as before, with one additional transport judge.

sentences.zh: 國初，設平陽府以征課程之利。

translations.literal: At the founding of the dynasty, Pingyang Prefecture was established to collect revenue.
translations.idiomatic: At the dynasty's founding, Pingyang Prefecture was established to collect tax revenue.

sentences.zh: 中統二年，改置轉運司，置提舉解鹽司。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhongtong, a transport commission was established, and the Jie Salt Intendant Office was set up.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhongtong, a transport commission was established along with the Jie Salt Intendant Office.

sentences.zh: 至元二年，罷運司，命有司掌其務，尋復置轉運司。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhiyuan, the transport commission was abolished and the relevant offices were ordered to manage its affairs; soon the transport commission was restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhiyuan, the transport commission was abolished and its affairs assigned to the relevant offices; the transport commission was soon restored.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，立陜西都轉運司，諸色稅課悉隸焉。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, the Shaanxi Director-General Transport Commission was established, and all categories of tax revenue came under its jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year, the Shaanxi Director-General Transport Commission was established, and all categories of tax revenue fell under its jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，置鹽運司，專掌鹽課，其餘課稅歸有司，解鹽司亦罷。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, a salt transport commission was established to manage salt revenue exclusively; the remaining tax revenue reverted to the relevant offices, and the Jie Salt Office was also abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year, a salt transport commission was established to manage salt revenue exclusively; other tax revenue reverted to the relevant offices, and the Jie Salt Office was abolished.

sentences.zh: 延祐六年，更為河東陜西等處都轉運鹽使司，隸省部。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yanyou, renamed the Hedong-Shaanxi and Other Places Director-General Salt Transport Commissioner's Office, subordinate to the ministry.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Yanyou, it was renamed the Hedong-Shaanxi and Other Places Director-General Salt Transport Commissioner's Office and placed under the ministry.

sentences.zh: 其屬三：

translations.literal: Its subordinates numbered three:
translations.idiomatic: It had three subordinate offices:

translations.idiomatic: The Jie Salt Saltern: one overseer, rank 9a;

translations.literal: one associate overseer, rank 9b.
translations.idiomatic: one associate overseer, rank 9b.

translations.idiomatic: The Hedong and Other Places Jie Salt Household Intendant Office: one chief intendant, rank 8b;

sentences.zh: 副提領一員，從九品。

translations.literal: one vice intendant, rank 9b.
translations.idiomatic: one vice intendant, rank 9b.

translations.literal: Anyi and Other Places Jie Salt Household Intendant Office, one chief intendant, rank 8b;
translations.idiomatic: The Anyi and Other Places Jie Salt Household Intendant Office: one chief intendant, rank 8b;

sentences.zh: 副提領一員，從九品。

translations.literal: one vice intendant, rank 9b.
translations.idiomatic: one vice intendant, rank 9b.

sentences.zh: 禮部，尚書三員，正三品；

translations.literal: Ministry of Rites — three ministers, rank 3a;
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites: three ministers, rank 3a;

sentences.zh: 侍郎二員，正四品；

translations.literal: two vice ministers, rank 4a;
translations.idiomatic: two vice ministers, rank 4a;

sentences.zh: 郎中二員，從五品；

translations.literal: two directors, rank 5b;
translations.idiomatic: two directors, rank 5b;

sentences.zh: 員外郎二員，從六品，掌天下禮樂、祭祀、朝會、燕享、貢舉之政令。

translations.literal: two vice directors, rank 6b, who managed the government's policies on rites and music, sacrifices, court assemblies, banquets, and the civil service examinations throughout the empire.
translations.idiomatic: two vice directors, rank 6b, who issued policies on rites and music, sacrifices, court assemblies, banquets, and civil service examinations empire-wide.

sentences.zh: 凡儀制損益之文，符印簡冊之信，神人封謚之法，忠孝貞義之褒，送迎聘好之節，文學僧道之事，婚姻繼續之辨，音藝膳供之物，悉以任之。

translations.literal: All documents on ritual regulations and their revisions, the authenticity of seals, credentials, and registers, methods for posthumous titles of spirits and men, honors for loyalty, filial piety, chastity, and righteousness, protocols for sending and receiving envoys and marriage alliances, matters of literature, Buddhism, and Daoism, disputes over marriage and succession, musical arts and provisions for feasts — all were entrusted to it.
translations.idiomatic: It held authority over ritual regulations and their revision, the authentication of seals, credentials, and registers, posthumous titles, honors for loyalty, filial piety, chastity, and righteousness, protocols for envoys and marriage alliances, literary and religious affairs, disputes over marriage and succession, and provisions for music and feasts.

sentences.zh: 世祖中統元年，以吏、戶、禮為左三部，置尚書二員，侍郎二員，郎中四員，員外郎六員，總領三部之事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhongtong under Shizu, Personnel, Revenue, and Rites became the Left Three Ministries — two ministers, two vice ministers, four directors, six vice directors — to oversee the affairs of all three ministries.
translations.idiomatic: In Shizu's first year of Zhongtong, Personnel, Revenue, and Rites were grouped as the Left Three Ministries with two ministers, two vice ministers, four directors, and six vice directors to oversee all three ministries.

sentences.zh: 至元元年，分立為吏禮部，尚書三員，侍郎仍二員，郎中仍四員，員外郎四員。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhiyuan, separated as the Ministry of Personnel and Rites — three ministers; vice ministers still two, directors still four, four vice directors.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhiyuan, Personnel and Rites were separated into the Ministry of Personnel and Rites: three ministers, two vice ministers, four directors, and four vice directors.

sentences.zh: 七年，別立禮部，尚書三員，侍郎一員，郎中二員，員外郎如舊。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, the Ministry of Rites was separately established — three ministers, one vice minister, two directors, vice directors as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, the Ministry of Rites was established separately: three ministers, one vice minister, two directors, and vice directors as before.

sentences.zh: 明年，又合為吏禮部。

translations.literal: The following year, again combined as the Ministry of Personnel and Rites.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, it was combined again as the Ministry of Personnel and Rites.

sentences.zh: 十三年，又別為禮部。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, again separated as the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, it was separated again as the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，六部尚書、侍郎、郎中、員外郎定以二員為額。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, the ministers, vice ministers, directors, and vice directors of the Six Ministries were fixed at two posts each.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year, the ministers, vice ministers, directors, and vice directors of the Six Ministries were each fixed at two posts.

sentences.zh: 成宗元貞元年，復增尚書一員，領會同館事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanzhen under Chengzong, one minister was added again to oversee the Hall of Joint Harmony.
translations.idiomatic: In Chengzong's first year of Yuanzhen, one minister was added again to oversee the Hall of Joint Harmony.

sentences.zh: 主事二員，蒙古必阇赤二人，令史一十九人，回回令史二人，怯裏馬赤一人，知印二人，奏差十二人，典吏三人。

translations.literal: Two section chiefs, two Mongol bitichi, nineteen clerks, two Muslim clerks, one keshig, two seal keepers, twelve memorial couriers, three record keepers.
translations.idiomatic: Staff included two section chiefs, two Mongol bitichi, nineteen clerks, two Muslim clerks, one keshig guard, two seal keepers, twelve memorial couriers, and three record keepers.

sentences.zh: 其屬附見：

translations.literal: Subordinates are appended below:
translations.idiomatic: Subordinate offices are listed below:

translations.literal: Auditor's Office of the Left Three Ministries, rank 8a — one auditor, who managed the revenue and expenditure accounts of the Personnel, Revenue, and Rites ministries.
translations.idiomatic: The Auditor's Office of the Left Three Ministries, rank 8a, had one auditor who managed the revenue and expenditure accounts of the Personnel, Revenue, and Rites ministries.

sentences.zh: 典吏八人。

translations.literal: Eight record keepers.
translations.idiomatic: Eight record keepers.

sentences.zh: 侍儀司，秩正四品，掌凡朝會、即位、冊後、建儲、奉上尊號及外國朝覲之禮。

translations.literal: Directorate of Ceremonial Protocol, rank 4a, which managed all rites for court assemblies, enthronements, investiture of empresses, establishment of heirs apparent, presentation of honorific titles, and audiences with foreign envoys.
translations.idiomatic: The Directorate of Ceremonial Protocol, rank 4a, managed rites for court assemblies, enthronements, investiture of empresses, establishment of heirs apparent, presentation of honorific titles, and audiences with foreign envoys.

sentences.zh: 至元八年始置。

translations.literal: First established in the eighth year of Zhiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: It was first established in the eighth year of Zhiyuan.

sentences.zh: 左右侍儀奉御二員，禮部侍郎知侍儀事一員，引進使知侍儀事一員，左右侍儀使二員，左右直侍儀使二員，左右侍儀副使二員，左右侍儀僉事二員，引進副使、侍儀令、承奉班都知、尚衣局大使各一員。

translations.literal: Two left and right ceremonial attendants, one vice minister of Rites overseeing ceremonial protocol, one usher overseeing ceremonial protocol, two left and right ceremonial commissioners, two left and right direct ceremonial commissioners, two left and right vice ceremonial commissioners, two left and right ceremonial assessors, and one each of usher vice commissioner, ceremonial director, director of the Attendance Corps, and commissioner of the Imperial Wardrobe Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: There were two left and right ceremonial attendants; one vice minister of Rites and one usher each oversaw ceremonial protocol; two left and right ceremonial commissioners, two direct ceremonial commissioners, two vice ceremonial commissioners, and two ceremonial assessors; and one each of usher vice commissioner, ceremonial director, director of the Attendance Corps, and commissioner of the Imperial Wardrobe Bureau.

sentences.zh: 十二年，省左侍儀奉御，通曰左右侍儀。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, the left ceremonial attendant was abolished; the title was unified as left and right ceremonial attendants.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year, the left ceremonial attendant was abolished and the title unified as left and right ceremonial attendants.

sentences.zh: 省引進副使及侍儀令、尚衣使等員，改置通事舍人十四員。

translations.literal: The usher vice commissioner and ceremonial director, Imperial Wardrobe commissioner, and other posts were abolished; fourteen interpreter ushers were established in their place.
translations.idiomatic: The usher vice commissioner, ceremonial director, Imperial Wardrobe commissioner, and related posts were abolished and replaced with fourteen interpreter ushers.

sentences.zh: 三十年，減通事舍人七員為侍儀舍人。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year, seven interpreter ushers were reduced and redesignated as ceremonial ushers.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year, seven interpreter ushers were reduced and redesignated as ceremonial ushers.

sentences.zh: 大德十一年，升秩正三品。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Dade, promoted to rank 3a.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Dade, it was promoted to rank 3a.

sentences.zh: 至大二年，置典簿一員。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhida, one registry officer was established.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhida, one registry officer was established.

sentences.zh: 延祐七年，定置侍儀使四員。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Yanyou, four ceremonial commissioners were fixed in the establishment.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Yanyou, four ceremonial commissioners were fixed in the establishment.

sentences.zh: 至治元年，增置通事舍人六員、侍儀舍人四員。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhizhi, six interpreter ushers and four ceremonial ushers were added.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhizhi, six interpreter ushers and four ceremonial ushers were added.

sentences.zh: 其後定置侍儀使四員，正三品；

translations.literal: Thereafter the fixed establishment was four ceremonial commissioners, rank 3a;
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the fixed establishment was four ceremonial commissioners, rank 3a;

translations.literal: two ushers overseeing ceremonial protocol, rank 4a.
translations.idiomatic: two ushers overseeing ceremonial protocol, rank 4a.

translations.idiomatic: Leadership officials: one registry officer, rank 7b.

translations.literal: Subordinate officials: one director of the Attendance Corps, rank 7a;
translations.idiomatic: Subordinate officials: one director of the Attendance Corps, rank 7a;

sentences.zh: 通事舍人一十六員，從七品；

translations.literal: sixteen interpreter ushers, rank 7b;
translations.idiomatic: sixteen interpreter ushers, rank 7b;

translations.literal: fourteen ceremonial ushers, rank 9b.
translations.idiomatic: fourteen ceremonial ushers, rank 9b.

translations.literal: Clerical staff: two clerks, one translator clerk, one interpreter, one seal keeper.
translations.idiomatic: Clerical staff included two clerks, one translator clerk, one interpreter, and one seal keeper.

sentences.zh: 其屬法物庫，秩五品，掌大禮法物。

translations.literal: Subordinate to it was the Repository of Ritual Implements, rank 5, which managed ritual implements for major ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: Subordinate to it was the Repository of Ritual Implements, rank 5, which managed ritual implements for major ceremonies.

translations.idiomatic: two chief stewards, rank 8a.

translations.idiomatic: The Direct Command of the Honored Guard held rank 4b.

sentences.zh: 掌控鶴六百餘戶，及儀衞之事。

translations.idiomatic: It controlled more than six hundred crane-controller households and managed ceremonial guard affairs.

translations.idiomatic: It was first established in the third year of Zhiyuan.

translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yuanzhen it was again promoted to rank 3a.

translations.idiomatic: In the second year the controller was renamed commissioner.

translations.idiomatic: The Repository of Ceremonial Escort, rank 7b.

translations.idiomatic: It managed ceremonial guards and weapons.

translations.literal: one commissioner, rank 7b;
translations.idiomatic: one commissioner, rank 7b;

translations.literal: one vice commissioner, rank 8b.
translations.idiomatic: one vice commissioner, rank 8b.
